title: SunPath Solar Lease Production Guarantee: Annual Reconciliation and Shortfall Credit
content:
**Performance guarantee terms of the SunPath Solar Lease.**

At the end of each lease year — each production reconciliation period of the system size's length in months — the system's metered production for that lease year is compared with the guaranteed production for that lease year.

**Guaranteed production.** The guaranteed production for a lease year is the system size's guaranteed share, in percent, of the estimated annual production reduced by the system size's yearly degradation percent for each lease year after the first, rounded to the nearest kWh. In the first lease year no degradation reduction applies, so the guaranteed production is the guaranteed share of the estimated first-year production.

**Shortfall credit.** Where the metered production is below the guaranteed production, the shortfall in kWh is credited at the system size's credit per kWh, rounded half up to the cent, and the credit for a lease year is never above the system size's annual credit cap. Where the metered production equals or exceeds the guaranteed production there is no shortfall and no credit. The credit for a lease year is therefore the lower of two amounts: the shortfall in kWh multiplied by the credit per kWh, and the annual credit cap.

**Production above the guarantee.** Production above the guaranteed production earns nothing and does not carry forward to another lease year.

**Lessee-requested downtime.** Shortfall caused by system downtime the lessee requested — removal of the system for roof work — is excluded.

**What the records show.** Each reconciled lease year is recorded with its metered production and its guaranteed production in kWh; a production guarantee credit is recorded once for the lease year it relates to, and it reduces the lease balance.

## Worked examples on hypothetical figures

The figures are invented for illustration and are not the figures of any SunPath size: estimated first-year production 6100 kWh, guaranteed share 90 percent, yearly degradation 0.5 percent, credit $0.30 per kWh, annual credit cap $500.00.

| Lease year | Guaranteed production | Metered production | Shortfall | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First | 90 percent of 6100 kWh is 5490 kWh | 5240 kWh | 250 kWh | 250 multiplied by $0.30 is $75.00 |
| Second | 6100 kWh reduced by 0.5 percent is 6069.5 kWh; 90 percent of that is 5462.55, rounded to 5463 kWh | 5500 kWh | None | $0.00; the 37 kWh above the guarantee earn nothing and do not carry forward |
| First, alternative outcome | 5490 kWh | 3490 kWh | 2000 kWh | 2000 multiplied by $0.30 is $600.00, above the cap, so the credit is $500.00 |

## Points of judgement

- The guarantee for a lease year is computed for that lease year alone; a surplus in one year neither raises nor offsets the guarantee or the shortfall of another.
- The cap is a ceiling on one lease year's credit, applied to the credit for that year.
- The comparison uses metered production for the lease year, measured over the reconciliation period.
